26 Which list shows electromagnetic waves in order of increasing frequency?
A
radio waves → gamma rays → ultraviolet → infra-red
B
radio waves → infra-red → ultraviolet → gamma rays
C
ultraviolet → gamma rays → radio waves → infra-red
D
ultraviolet → infra-red → radio waves → gamma rays

hints: Notice the four named regions: radio waves, infra-red, ultraviolet and gamma rays - recall which end of the spectrum has the lowest frequency.
Connect frequency to the spectrum order using $c = f\lambda$: all EM waves travel at $c$ in vacuum, so lowest frequency means longest wavelength.
Check each list from left to right for increasing frequency, remembering that infra-red is next to visible on the low-frequency side and ultraviolet is on the high-frequency side.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: the four regions must be placed in order of increasing frequency $f$, meaning smallest $f$ first and largest $f$ last.
Recall the EM spectrum in order of increasing frequency: radio waves, microwaves, infra-red, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays.

Apply this to the four given regions: radio waves has the lowest $f$ with wavelength of order metres or more, then infra-red with wavelength near $10^{-5} \text{ m}$, then ultraviolet with wavelength near $10^{-8} \text{ m}$, then gamma rays with the highest $f$ and wavelength below $10^{-11} \text{ m}$.
Compare each list: only the sequence radio waves $\rightarrow$ infra-red $\rightarrow$ ultraviolet $\rightarrow$ gamma rays increases in $f$ at every step.

A.explanation: Radio waves are lowest frequency but gamma rays are highest frequency, so gamma rays cannot come second in increasing frequency.

B.explanation: Frequency increases from radio waves to infra-red to ultraviolet to gamma rays, matching the EM spectrum order.

C.explanation: Ultraviolet has much higher frequency than radio waves and infra-red, so it cannot be first in increasing frequency.

D.explanation: Infra-red has higher frequency than radio waves, so infra-red cannot follow ultraviolet then come before radio waves in increasing order.
